tone_statements.citation: Barreteau, Daniel & Yves Le Bleis. 1990. Lexique mafa: langue de la famille tchadique parlee au Cameroun. (Etudes tchadiques, Monographies.) Paris: ORSTOM / Geuthner. 473 pp. IRD Horizon fdi:34119.
tone_statements.quote: Il Y a une opposition de deux tons ponctuels haut / bas. Le ton haut (H) est marqué par un accent, le ton bas (B) est non-marqué : vézay "épervier" vézay "derrière" … Il y a très peu de paires minimales de ce genre dans le lexique. Considérant les deux derniers tons d'un nom, on peut distinguer des schèmes tonals isotones (H-H, B-B) ou hétérotone (H-B). Lexicalement, aucune schème ne se termine par une séquence bas-haut (B-H). Dans certaines constructions grammaticales apparait un ton modulé bas-haut (BH) sur la dernière syllabe.
tone_statements.translation: There is an opposition of two level (punctual) tones, high / low. The high tone (H) is marked with an accent, the low tone (B) is unmarked: vézay 'sparrowhawk' / vezay 'behind' … There are very few minimal pairs of this kind in the lexicon. Considering the last two tones of a noun, one can distinguish isotone (H-H, L-L) or heterotone (H-L) tonal schemes. Lexically, no scheme ends in a low-high (L-H) sequence. In certain grammatical constructions a modulated low-high (LH) tone appears on the last syllable.

tone_statements.translation: 2.3. Tones. The high tone is marked with an accent: á, while the low tone remains unmarked: a. A rising low-high tone is attested only in certain grammatical contexts (cf. Le Bleis 1985). The tonal schemes are limited in number.

tone_statements.summary: 2 level tones, H (marked with acute) vs L (unmarked); rising LH contour only in certain grammatical contexts; restricted inventory of lexical tone schemes.

sources.note: Nothing. 'Elements phonologiques' pp.15-20 covers syllable (CV, CVC, syllabic nasal), consonants, vowels/palatalisation-labialisation prosodies, and sec. 5 'Les tons' (p.20): two level tones H/L, nominal tone schemes H-H, B-B, H-B (no lexical B-H), grammatical rising BH on last syllable; morpho-phonology pp.20ff. gives tone raising/lowering/assimilation rules. No mention of stress/accent d'intensite anywhere in the book (only 'accent' = acute diacritic for H tone).

sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 6 'Les tons' (p.15-16 of the typescript; scanned poor): 'Dans la langue mafa, chaque centre de syllabe (voyelle ou nasale syllabique) porte une hauteur musicale determinee.. chaque syllabe est caracterisee par un ton propre. Deux registres tonals sont observes: haut et bas'; H marked by an acute accent, L unmarked; tones have low functional load in nouns, higher in verbs; tone schemes listed for 1-3 syllable words.

sources.note: Sec. 2.3 'Les tons' (p.168): high tone marked with an accent, low tone unmarked; a rising low-high tone occurs only in certain grammatical contexts (referring to Le Bleis 1985); tonal schemes are limited in number. Later (pp.185-190, on mofu-gudur and Chadic generally) argues tone schemes ('accent tonal') matter more than free tone combinations and that non-vocalised syllables bear tone, so Chadic languages look more like 'langues a accent' than 'langues a tons'.
